headline: OpenAI chief scientist suggests perplexity could be the basis for AI limits
body: A new blog post from OpenAI’s chief scientist Jakub Pachocki discusses potential limits on AI development, with a focus on perplexity. In his view, perplexity could provide the basis for “a shared benchmark for general intelligence,” which AI companies could then use to establish “common limits.”
note: Any speed limit needs a shared way to measure speed first, and Pachocki suggests perplexity for that job.

evidence.text: A new blog post from OpenAI’s chief scientist Jakub Pachocki discusses potential limits on AI development, with a focus on a measurement called perplexity.
So in his view, perplexity could provide the basis for “a shared benchmark for general intelligence,” which AI companies could then use to establish “common limits.”
But to establish a speed limit on AI development, you need to agree on how you measure speed.

Pachocki’s post — described by Altman as “the most important thing OpenAI has published in a while” — suggests perplexity (not to be confused with the company of the same name ) could be that measurement.
